question: What are nutrients mainly known as in nursing care?

options.A: Caloric restrictions required for managing chronic weight loss
options.B: Chemical substances in food needed for body function and repair
options.C: Medical supplements prescribed only during surgical recovery
options.D: Artificial additives used to preserve packaged hospital meals

explanation: You got this! Nutrients are simply the useful components in our food that give our bodies energy and help us grow and heal every day. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T003#GNS227_U1_T003_h1)

question: Why is the nurse often the first person to spot early signs of poor nutrition in a patient?

options.A: Nurses perform the initial admission assessments and spend the most direct time with patients
options.B: Nurses are legally responsible for preparing all hospital meal trays
options.C: Nurses hold advanced degrees in clinical biochemistry and food science
options.D: Nurses alone have the authority to prescribe therapeutic hospital diets

explanation: Spot on! Because you are right there at the bedside doing admissions and checking on patients constantly, you are in the best position to notice changes in their nutrition. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T003#GNS227_U1_T003_h1)

question: Which food nutrient is mainly responsible for body building and fighting off infections?
explanation: Great job! Proteins are made of amino acids, which act like the bricks and mortar of the body for repair, growth, and strong immunity. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T003#GNS227_U1_T003_h2)

question: A patient is healing from a major surgery and needs help repairing skin and tissues. Which nutrient should you encourage?
explanation: Well done! Surgical wounds need plenty of protein to rebuild skin, muscle, and internal structures back to health. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T003#GNS227_U1_T003_h2)

question: How do water-soluble vitamins behave differently from fat-soluble vitamins in the body?

options.A: Water-soluble vitamins can be stored in the liver in large toxic amounts
options.B: Fat-soluble vitamins play no role in normal human physiological processes
options.C: Water-soluble vitamins are excreted in urine and require more frequent intake
options.D: Fat-soluble vitamins cannot be absorbed without adequate daily hydration

explanation: You're doing great! Water-soluble vitamins dissolve in body fluids, meaning any extra gets peed out. That's why we need a fresh supply of them regularly in our meals. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T003#GNS227_U1_T003_h3)

question: What is the main job of minerals like sodium and potassium in our bodies?

options.A: Regulating fluid balance and supporting nerve and muscle function
options.B: Acting as organic enzymes to speed up chemical digestion
options.C: Providing the structural framework for red blood cell hemoglobin
options.D: Serving as the body's primary emergency source of stored calories

explanation: Correct! Electrolytes like sodium and potassium keep our body fluids balanced and help our nerves and muscles work smoothly without cramping. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T003#GNS227_U1_T003_h3)

question: Roughly what percentage of a healthy adult's body weight is water?
explanation: Exactly! Water is our most abundant component, making up about 60 percent of a grown adult's weight. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T003#GNS227_U1_T003_h4)

question: Why are elderly patients much more likely to get seriously dehydrated than younger adults?

options.A: They consume strictly dry foods with zero moisture content
options.B: Their kidneys completely stop producing urine as they age
options.C: They often have a reduced sense of thirst and less total body water reserve
options.D: Their skin absorbs environmental moisture instead of retaining internal fluids

explanation: Spot on! As people age, their natural feeling of thirst gets weaker, and they hold less water in their bodies, so they can dry out before they even realize they are thirsty. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T003#GNS227_U1_T003_h4)

question: In which part of our digestive system does most nutrient absorption happen?
explanation: You got it! The small intestine has tiny finger-like folds (villi) that create a huge surface area to soak up all the good nutrients into our bloodstream. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T003#GNS227_U1_T003_h5)

question: What is the main difference between anabolism and catabolism?

options.A: Anabolism produces waste products, while catabolism produces vitamins
options.B: Anabolism occurs in the stomach, while catabolism happens in the liver
options.C: Anabolism deals only with fats, while catabolism processes water
options.D: Anabolism builds up body tissues, while catabolism breaks down molecules for energy

explanation: Well remembered! Think of anabolism as building up (like construction) and catabolism as breaking down (like demolition to release energy). [learn more](GNS227_U1_T003#GNS227_U1_T003_h5)

question: Which of these measurements is a standard part of checking a patient's nutrition using body measurements (anthropometry)?
explanation: Correct! Anthropometry simply means measuring the physical body—height, weight, and BMI are the most common ways we do this in the clinic. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T003#GNS227_U1_T003_h6)

question: When helping a Nigerian patient plan a healthy, balanced local diet, which food combination is best?

options.A: High-fat fried snacks consumed without any protein or vegetable source
options.B: Yam or cassava served with beans, fish, and green leafy vegetable soup
options.C: Strictly white refined sugar dissolved in large quantities of clean water
options.D: Imported processed canned foods supplemented with synthetic energy drinks

explanation: Wonderful! Combining local energy staples like yam or cassava with protein (beans, fish) and nutrient-rich green leaves gives a complete, culturally wonderful meal. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T003#GNS227_U1_T003_h6)

question: Which of the following is a well-known childhood illness caused by a serious lack of protein in the diet?
explanation: You're right! Kwashiorkor happens when children don't get enough protein, often leading to swollen bellies and muscle wasting. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T003#GNS227_U1_T003_h7)

question: Why can taking very large megadoses of fat-soluble vitamins be dangerous?

options.A: Fat-soluble vitamins are stored in the body and can accumulate to toxic levels
options.B: The body attacks fat-soluble vitamins as foreign bacteria and triggers shock
options.C: Excess fat-soluble vitamins instantly turn into dangerous trans fats
options.D: High doses immediately cause total kidney failure by dissolving water in blood

explanation: Spot on! Because fat-soluble vitamins get stored in our body fat and liver instead of being peed out, taking too many over time can build up to dangerous levels. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T003#GNS227_U1_T003_h7)
